kids: 📚 GCSE Maths now has 123 kinds of question across seven topics, and your estimated grade from mock papers
items: 📚 GCSE Foundation content: 99 new question types across number, algebra, graphs (new), ratio and rates, geometry, measures (new) and probability and statistics — each with hints, a worked method and lessons. Graphs and tables are drawn on screen; answers can be expressions, both roots of a quadratic, coordinates, ratios or prime-factor form.
🎯 Estimated GCSE grade: shown at the top of the page and in Grown-ups → Readiness, from the last three mock papers, using AQA’s June 2025 grade boundaries as a guide.
📝 GCSE mock papers are now 25 questions in 90 minutes, scored in marks, for AQA, Edexcel and OCR.
🔧 Fixes: tidier algebra (no “1x” or “+ 0”), correct rounding of numbers ending in 5, and graphs with different scales on each axis.

kids: 🌙 GCSE and A level get their own look: “Night study” (with a light theme), your own character, XP levels and 🎨 Customise
items: 🌙 The senior look for GCSE and A level (automatic from Year 10; grown-ups can change it in Grown-ups → Plan): a calm night-city design with a ☀️/🌙 light theme, a greeting instead of the comic title, and calmer wording — Submit, “✓ Correct”, XP and levels, no football or comic words. Younger children see no change.

🎨 Customise replaces the Shop for older students: outfits (hoodies, bomber, denim, puffer, varsity), trainers, accessories (headphones, glasses, cap, beanie, smartwatch), desk and room items, backdrops, frames, titles earned by mastery and a focus-sounds perk. Ten hobbies (football analytics, F1, music production, gaming, fashion, coding, space, film, travel, fitness) each set the accent colour and add their own items.
🧑 A new character with natural proportions, drawn with your own skin tone, hair and head covering; “Your space” shows your desk set-up.
💳 Credits to spend are the same points as before; XP (everything you have ever earned) sets your level and never goes down. Purchases are checked when progress is reopened.

kids: 📐 GCSE Maths has started: proper maths on screen, algebra answers, graphs and a formula sheet
items: 🎓 New exams: GCSE Maths for AQA, Pearson Edexcel and OCR, with Foundation or Higher chosen in Grown-ups → Plan and each board’s three papers in Mock exam (Paper 1 non-calculator for AQA and Edexcel). This first release has 24 GCSE question types plus KS3 revision; many more follow.

✍️ Algebra answers: type an expression (e.g. 6x + 10) and it is marked by its value, with a nudge if it needs expanding, factorising, a surd or standard form. Quadratics take both answers in any order; simultaneous equations take (x, y).
📈 Proper maths display (fractions, powers, roots) and graphs, plus a 📐 formula sheet to revise from (the board gives you its own in the exam). Questions say whether a calculator is needed.
🎨 Grown-ups → Plan has a Look setting: automatic (a new senior look from Year 10 — arriving in the next version), children’s, or senior.

kids: 🧒 Years 1 and 2: picture questions — clocks, coins, number lines and more — that you can tap and hear read aloud. 🧑‍🎓 Years 7, 8 and 9: KS3 maths, from negative numbers to Pythagoras
items: 🧒 New exams: Year 1 and Year 2 maths (KS1). Picture questions (clock faces, coins, number lines, tens and ones, arrays, fraction shapes, counters), answer buttons to tap in practice (a wrong tap leaves the others open), and questions read aloud when sound is on. 36 question types. Year 2 has KS1-style Papers 1 (arithmetic) and 2 (reasoning). Year 3 now includes some KS1 revision.

🧑‍🎓 New exams: Year 7, Year 8 and Year 9 maths (KS3): five topics — negatives, powers and primes; equations and sequences; ratio and percentages; geometry (polygons, circles, Pythagoras, bearings); probability and statistics — 46 question types held back by year, with lessons and explainers.
🎓 13+ Common Entrance now includes the KS3 topics too.

kids: 🧠 SATs reasoning papers, Year 3, 4 and 5 practice, and a times-tables check with a 6-second timer — just like the real one
items: 🏆 KS2 SATs mocks now offer all three papers: Paper 1 arithmetic (36 questions, 30 minutes) and Papers 2 and 3 reasoning (24 questions, 40 minutes each), all scored in marks. Choose the paper in Mock exam.

🧠 Five new SATs-level reasoning topics (place value, rounding, Roman numerals, negative numbers; money, time and measures; angles, shape and position; tables, charts and averages; word problems) — 47 question types with hints, worked methods, lessons and explainers. Charts and timetables are drawn on screen.

📅 New exams: Year 3, Year 4 and Year 5 maths (national curriculum practice — nothing from later years and no 11+ puzzles) and the Year 4 multiplication tables check (25 questions, 6 seconds each, moves on by itself).
👪 Grown-ups → Plan: Year 4 children get “➕ Add the times-tables check”. Focus topics only include topics the child’s year can actually practise.

kids: ➕ KS2 SATs practice: five new arithmetic missions (adding, multiplying, dividing, fractions, percentages) and a Paper 1 mock — 36 questions in 30 minutes, scored in marks like the real test
items: 🎓 New exam: KS2 SATs (Year 6). Practice and focus topics follow the national tests, with 36 new arithmetic question types (column methods, long multiplication and long division, decimals, negative numbers, fraction calculations, percentages, order of operations, squares and cubes) — each with three hints, a worked method, a Learn mission and “Explain it simply”.
🏆 SATs Paper 1 mock: 36 arithmetic questions in 30 minutes, scored in marks (long multiplication and long division are worth 2, as in the real paper).

📅 Grown-ups → Plan: a School year picker (questions taught after that year are held back) and, for Year 6 children, “➕ Add KS2 SATs — 13 May 2027”. Key dates now include the SATs maths days, results and the Year 4 times-tables check.
🔧 Fix: a 50-question 11+ mock was saved as out of 40 when progress was reopened.

🎯 Focus areas follow the exam automatically — when the app opens and whenever the exam changes — until a grown-up chooses their own in Grown-ups → Focus areas. The Focus areas tab says which it is, and “↺ Follow the exam again” goes back to automatic.

kids: 🎯 When your exam changes, your questions, Focus Zone and today’s plan change with it straight away
items: 🎓 Changing the exam in Grown-ups → Plan now refreshes the child’s page at once: the question on screen is replaced by one from the new exam, focus topics move to the new exam (unless you chose your own), and today’s plan, Next best thing and the mock length follow. A mock in progress starts again at the new exam’s length.
🔧 The Fix-it list no longer brings back question types from a different exam.
📱 On phones and tablets the exam plan shows one card per test (no sideways scrolling), and on phones the dashboard tabs sit in one scrolling strip so the content has room.

🤖 Exam information is now AI-maintained: the exam-watch agent’s checked updates (key dates and new questions) go live automatically, and Key dates shows “Kept up to date by an AI agent — last checked …”.

kids: 🧭 A refreshed tour, and your Focus Zone now names your own exam
items: 🛡️ Deleting a player now needs their name typed exactly (plus the grown-up passphrase), and deleted players go to a ♻️ recycle bin for 30 days — restore them from “Who’s playing?” with all their progress.
🪐 Starlane now always opens from its own site (stuartokin.github.io/Starlane); the copy built into ApolloMaths has been removed, so the app is smaller and faster.
🚀 Maths questions sent to Starlane now use the child’s own name and theme (never “Apollo”).
⭐ The Focus Zone names each child’s own exam, and existing players on other exams get focus topics from their exam (unless a grown-up chose them).
👪 The family-codes reminder moved from the children’s screen to the Grown-ups button (⚠️). Setup adds “🙂 I’ll design my own” for the character.
🎓 The guided tour and Help are updated for the new layout — the tour now visits every area (16 steps).
🤖 Exam watch: it now proposes key dates from official sources (shown with ✨ once you merge) and drafts whole question generators, each run 50 times in a sandbox and checked by a second solve.
🧩 engine.html: the question engine on its own, so the Starlane site can offer exam practice.
